capabilities_rationale: Two of these are deliberately stronger than scripts/audit_skill_safety.py derives, and the gap is the interesting part. The auditor reports network=none and process_execution=none for this bundle because both capabilities are exercised through third-party SDKs whose names are not in its import tables: scripts/evaluation.py imports the `anthropic` client and calls the Claude API, and scripts/connections.py imports `mcp` and calls stdio_client(StdioServerParameters(command=..., args=..., env=...)), which launches an arbitrary command as a child process. An AST that matches on module names cannot see a capability that lives behind a dependency. Declaring the auditor's weaker answer would have passed CI and been false, so the stronger and true values are declared here and the resulting CAP-OVERDECLARED warnings are pinned in docs/safety-allowlist.json with this reasoning. FILESYSTEM 'workspace-write': the evaluation harness writes report files beside its inputs.

tested_platforms.notes: Vendored for display in this catalogue. No trigger suite has been run against evals/test-cases.json on any platform, and no MCP server has been built end-to-end with it here. The prompts in evals/ describe the skill's intended trigger surface; they have never been executed as a measurement.
tested_platforms.currency_caveat: Recorded as NOT_RUN deliberately rather than left absent. attestation_status is DRAFT for the same reason: this repository has read this skill and derived its capabilities, and has not evaluated it.

security_audit.method: This repository's own third-party verifier was run over the bundle as an untrusted stranger's skill. Verdict: NO KNOWN FINDINGS -- 0 critical, 0 high, 0 warn, 5 info, over 10 files (7 prose, 2 python, 1 text-data). Note that the verifier derived network=outbound here where the auditor derived none: its module table includes asyncio, which scripts/evaluation.py imports. The two tools disagreeing on the same file is not a defect in either -- the verifier is deliberately the broader of the two because it is pointed at strangers' code -- but it is why the declaration above was checked against the source by hand rather than copied from either tool.
security_audit.scope_caveat: A static scan of vendored code, and static scans do not follow calls into dependencies. scripts/requirements.txt pulls `mcp` and `anthropic` from PyPI; nothing here has audited those packages, and running this skill's evaluation harness runs them.
